rule.name: No contractions
rule.message: Write the words in full. No contractions.
rule.example: You don't need this file.
If you're connecting, use TCP.
You do not need this file.
sqlpipe's IP is in the config.

rule.name: No semicolons
rule.message: Write two sentences, or name the relation.
rule.example: Start the tool; then read the log.
Start the tool. Then read the log.

rule.name: No em-dashes
rule.message: Write two sentences, or use a comma.
rule.example: The tool is fast—it also works.
The tool is fast. It also works.

rule.name: Only can, will, must
rule.message: Use can, will, or must. State the requirement exactly.
rule.example: You should restart the service.
You must restart the service.

rule.name: Active voice
rule.message: Use the active voice. Say who does the action.
rule.example: The log was written by the worker.
The worker wrote the log.

rule.name: Simple tenses only
rule.message: Use the simple past. Say when it happened.
rule.example: The job has completed.
The job completed.

rule.name: No -ing after a comma
rule.message: Start a new sentence instead of the -ing phrase.
rule.example: The tool runs, making it easy.
The tool runs. It is easy.
The walkthrough (accounts, VPC, secrets, troubleshooting) is in the guide.
The guide covers billing, troubleshooting, and support for each environment.
The guide covers billing, troubleshooting and support for each environment.
The guide covers billing, troubleshooting or support for each environment.

rule.name: make sure that
rule.example: Make sure the file exists.
Make sure that the file exists.

rule.name: Condition before command
rule.message: Put the condition first: "If the build fails, read the log."
rule.example: Read the log if the build fails.
If the build fails, read the log.

rule.name: use, not leverage
rule.example: Utilize the registry file.
Use the registry file.

rule.name: to, not in order to
rule.example: Run the tool in order to build the file.
Run the tool to build the file.

rule.name: before, not prior to
rule.example: Read the file prior to the upgrade.
Read the file before the upgrade.

rule.name: make sure that, not ensure
rule.example: Ensure the file exists.
Make sure that the file exists.

rule.name: function, not functionality
rule.example: Add the functionality first.
Add the function first.

rule.name: you can, not enables you to
rule.example: The tool enables you to build the file.
You can build the file with the tool.

rule.name: help, not facilitate
rule.example: The tool facilitates the build.
The tool helps the build.

rule.name: read, not delve into
rule.example: Delve into the config file.
Read the config file.

rule.name: for, not when it comes to
rule.example: When it comes to builds, use the tool.
For builds, use the tool.

rule.name: if, not in the event that
rule.example: In the event that the build fails, read the log.
If the build fails, read the log.

rule.name: because, not due to the fact that
rule.example: Due to the fact that the port is closed, the tool fails.
Because the port is not open, the tool fails.

rule.name: no and/or
rule.message: Pick one. Or write "X, or Y, or both".
rule.example: Set the flag and/or the port.
Set the flag, or the port, or both.

rule.name: e.g.
rule.message: Write "for example", or name the items.
rule.example: Set the flag, e.g. the port.
Set the flag, for example the port.

rule.name: i.e.
rule.message: Write "that is", or name the items.
rule.example: Set the flag, i.e. the port.
Set the flag, that is the port.

rule.name: etc.
rule.example: Set the flag, etc.
Set the flag or the port.

rule.name: by default, not out of the box
rule.example: The tool works out of the box.
The tool works by default.

rule.name: internally, not under the hood
rule.example: Under the hood, the tool builds a file.
Internally, the tool builds a file.

rule.name: make simpler, not streamline
rule.message: Write make simpler or make faster.
rule.example: The tool streamlines the build.
The tool makes the build simpler.

rule.name: many, not plethora
rule.example: The file has a plethora of rows.
The file has many rows.

rule.name: corrects, not addresses the issue
rule.message: Write corrects the fault or removes the error.
rule.example: The tool addresses the issue.
The tool corrects the fault.

rule.name: important, not pivotal
rule.example: The flag is crucial.
The flag is important.

rule.name: no tapestry, testament, synergy
rule.example: The design is a testament to the team.
The design shows the work of the team.

rule.name: interaction, not interplay
rule.example: The interplay of the two tools is complex.
The interaction of the two tools is complex.

rule.name: complex, not intricate
rule.example: The config is intricate.
The config is complex.

rule.name: delete vibrant, nuanced, multifaceted
rule.message: Delete it, or name the parts.
rule.example: The tool is nuanced.
The tool reads three file types.

rule.name: area, not realm or landscape
rule.example: In the realm of builds, use the tool.
In the area of builds, use the tool.

rule.name: new, not groundbreaking
rule.example: The tool is groundbreaking.
The tool is new.

rule.name: say what changes, not transformative
rule.example: The tool is transformative.
The tool cuts the build time in half.

rule.name: change, not revolutionize
rule.example: The tool revolutionizes the build.
The tool changes the build.

rule.name: show, not showcase
rule.example: The log showcases the error.
The log shows the error.

rule.name: help, not foster
rule.example: The tool fosters growth.
The tool supports growth.

rule.name: use, not harness
rule.example: Harness the API.
Use the API.

rule.name: improve, not enhance
rule.example: The tool enhances the build.
The tool improves the build.

rule.name: increase, not elevate
rule.example: The tool elevates the speed.
The tool increases the speed.

rule.name: also, not furthermore
rule.example: Furthermore, the tool reads the log.
The tool also reads the log.

rule.name: start, not embark
rule.example: Embark on the build.
Start the build.

rule.name: careful, not meticulous
rule.example: The tool checks the file meticulously.
The tool checks the file carefully.

rule.name: full, not holistic
rule.example: The tool gives a holistic view.
The tool gives a full view.

rule.name: model, not paradigm
rule.example: The tool changes the paradigm.
The tool changes the model.

rule.name: has, not boasts
rule.example: The tool boasts a log.
The tool has a log.

rule.name: but, not that being said
rule.example: The tool works. That being said, it is slow.
The tool works, but it is slow.

rule.name: but, not notwithstanding
rule.example: Notwithstanding the log, the tool fails.
The log exists, but the tool fails.

rule.name: delete empty adverbs
rule.message: Delete it. It carries no fact.
rule.example: The tool works seamlessly.
The tool works.

rule.name: delete just
rule.message: Delete it. It carries no fact.
rule.example: The tool just works.
The tool works.

rule.name: delete empty adjectives
rule.message: Delete it, or give the measurable property.
rule.example: The tool is robust.
The tool retries three times, then stops.

rule.name: delete it is worth noting
rule.example: It is worth noting that the tool is slow.
The tool is slow.

rule.name: delete it is important to
rule.example: It is important to read the log.
Read the log.

rule.name: delete is designed to
rule.example: The tool is designed to read logs.
The tool reads logs.

rule.name: delete aims to
rule.example: The tool aims to read logs.
The tool reads logs.

rule.name: state the condition, not as needed
rule.example: Restart the tool as needed.
Restart the tool every day.

rule.name: say what it does, not gracefully handles
rule.message: Say what the tool does: "retries three times, then stops".
rule.example: The tool gracefully handles the error.
The tool retries three times, then stops.

rule.name: delete in conclusion
rule.example: In conclusion, the tool works.
The tool works.

rule.name: delete in summary
rule.example: In summary, the tool works.
The tool works.

rule.name: delete at the end of the day
rule.example: At the end of the day, the tool works.
The tool works.

rule.name: give the location, not nestled
rule.example: The file is nestled in the folder.
The file sits in the folder.

rule.name: busy, not bustling
rule.example: The bustling market has many files.
The busy market has many files.

rule.name: delete I hope this helps
rule.example: I hope this helps. Read the log.
Read the log.

rule.name: delete let's dive in
rule.example: let's dive in. Read the log.
Read the log.
